stories.headline: Registry Center data breach of 600,000 records triggers political crisis for Ruginienė government
stories.summary: A cyberattack on Lithuania's Registry Center (Registrų centras) extracted personal data on approximately 600,000 residents, including home addresses of intelligence officers and diplomats. PM Ruginienė acknowledged knowing about the breach since early April but defended withholding public notification due to an ongoing pre-trial investigation; President Nausėda publicly rebuked her, calling the breach a hostile state cyberattack rather than an ordinary theft. Opposition leader Šimonytė and former prime ministers condemned the government's handling; VSD director Bridikis confirmed intelligence personnel were among victims; the Registry Center director resigned; and commentators warned the scandal left Ruginienė more politically vulnerable than at any prior point.

stories.headline: Russian drone hits Romanian apartment building; Lithuanian officials condemn and call for stronger NATO response
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck an apartment building in eastern Romania, injuring two people. Lithuanian PM Ruginienė, President Nausėda, and Foreign Minister Budrys each publicly condemned the incident and called on NATO to respond more decisively rather than accepting drone incursions as routine.

stories.headline: Germany inaugurates first permanent postwar brigade in Lithuania, marking historic NATO deployment
stories.summary: Germany formally inaugurated its 45th Armored Brigade in Lithuania — the first permanent full battle brigade deployed outside Germany since World War II. President Nausėda called it 'an exceptional event in our country's history,' and Defense Minister Kaunas noted Lithuania now spends 5.38% of GDP on defense, the highest NATO share.

stories.headline: Lithuania approves purchase of 936 Patria armored vehicles and forms new long-range drone warfare unit
stories.summary: Lithuania's State Defense Council authorized the Ministry of National Defence to purchase 936 Patria 6x6 armored personnel carriers from Finland, with a contract expected in 2027 and 300 vehicles arriving by 2030; President Nausėda conditioned the deal on Lithuanian industrial participation. Announced the same day, the Lithuanian Armed Forces also established a new centralized long-range autonomous drone unit (ANBO).

stories.headline: Baltic drone threat environment: Russia GPS spoofing warning and Latvia deploys anti-drone units to border
stories.summary: Lithuania's communications regulator warned that Russia has expanded GPS spoofing capacity from Kaliningrad to cover most of northeastern Europe. In parallel, Latvia announced deployment of mobile drone intercept teams to its Russian and Belarusian borders, citing drone incursions including an incident that forced Lithuanian lawmakers to shelter in Vilnius on May 20.

stories.summary: Lithuania's Seimas hosted the NATO Parliamentary Assembly's spring session, with President Nausėda, PM Ruginienė, NATO Deputy Secretary General Šekerinska, and EU Defense Commissioner Andrius Kubilius among the speakers; Ukrainian officials used the forum to press for urgent air defense reinforcement.

stories.summary: Media investigations revealed that at least ten Seimas members declared six-figure euro sums held in cash, with Dawn of Nemunas leaders prominent among them. President Nausėda said holding cash is a personal choice provided the origin is documented and lawful.

stories.summary: PM Ruginienė called the ongoing law enforcement investigation into cigarette contraband transported via meteorological balloons from Belarus 'unprecedented,' said the current wave of arrests is not the end of the case, and framed the balloon activity as a hybrid operation alongside commercial smuggling.

stories.headline: PM rules out tax increases despite rising inflation and finance minister property tax hint
stories.summary: PM Ruginienė publicly stated there are currently no discussions about tax increases, pushing back against comments by the finance minister that property taxes could sustainably raise revenue. She said the government's priority is income growth rather than new levies, and forecasted inflation could reach 5% annually.

stories.summary: Newly elected LSDP chairman Mindaugas Sinkevičius publicly deflected speculation that he would take over from Ruginienė as prime minister during this Seimas term, saying 'definitely not for now,' while not ruling out a future Vilnius move; PM Ruginienė tersely told him to focus on party affairs.

stories.headline: US military forces train Lithuanian Riflemen and test counter-drone Stryker system in Lithuania
stories.summary: US Army cavalry scouts from 1st Battalion, 12th Cavalry trained Lithuania's 20,000-strong Lithuanian Riflemen's Union in close-quarters battle at Pabradė. Separately, a US Maneuver Short-Range Air Defense Stryker vehicle fired its 30mm cannon against aerial targets during Project Flytrap counter-drone testing in Lithuania.
